models_evaluated: Logistic regression model for 2-year post-resection mortality (developed on 2011–2015, frozen)

links.outcome: Calibration drift of frozen prediction model over time despite stable discrimination
links.effect: Discrimination stable (AUC 0.76 development; 0.74 and 0.75 later eras) but calibration intercept drifted to -0.54 and -0.31, 95% CIs excluding zero, with over-prediction.
links.quote: Discrimination remained stable (optimism-corrected development AUC 0.76; later eras 0.74 and 0.75), but calibration drifted: the intercept became − 0.54 and − 0.31, both 95% CIs excluding zero, with over-prediction in both access strata.

links.outcome: Effect of contemporaneous vs stale intercept recalibration on calibration and discrimination
links.effect: Contemporaneous intercept recalibration restored calibration-in-the-large (predicted 19.2%→15.6%) without affecting discrimination; a correction estimated in the earlier era failed to transport and reversed bias direction.
links.quote: Contemporaneous intercept recalibration restored calibration-in-the-large (predicted 19.2%→15.6%) without affecting discrimination; a correction estimated in the earlier era failed to transport and reversed the direction of the bias.

links.outcome: Whether recalibrating with representative contemporaneous data fixes miscalibration
links.effect: Contemporaneous intercept recalibration restored calibration-in-the-large (predicted 19.2%→15.6%) without affecting discrimination; stale correction failed to transport.
links.quote: Contemporaneous intercept recalibration restored calibration-in-the-large (predicted 19.2%→15.6%) without affecting discrimination; a correction estimated in the earlier era failed to transport and reversed the direction of the bias.

links.outcome: Loss of calibration relative to original validation over a decade of static deployment
links.effect: Discrimination stable, but calibration intercept drifted (-0.54, -0.31) with over-prediction as baseline mortality fell from 20.5% to 15.6%.
links.quote: Discrimination-based validation can conceal clinically meaningful calibration drift.

unlisted_practices: Use calibration intercept as drift trigger and reference calibration slope to optimism-corrected deployment-time value rather than 1
